summary:
SOL 300 is a mission-driven, 3D interactive educational game designed to make the scientific, technological, and operational challenges of establishing and maintaining a research base on Mars accessible through immersive exploration and experiential learning.

Developed using Unreal Engine and Blender, the prototype allows players to control an astronaut from a third-person perspective, explore a realistically designed Martian research facility, and interact with environments representing essential space mission operations, including habitat management, greenhouse cultivation, scientific research, environmental data collection, and crew health.

The project addresses the challenge of transforming complex space exploration concepts into engaging, understandable learning experiences. Drawing inspiration from NASA technologies and missions, including Phoenix, Perseverance, and life-support systems, SOL 300 connects scientific knowledge with interactive, mission-oriented learning.

Our long-term vision is to develop SOL 300 into a modular educational simulation platform supporting scenario-based instruction, interdisciplinary STEM education, and future lunar and planetary exploration modules.

By bridging scientific research, interactive technology, and education, SOL 300 aims to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
details:
SOL 300 is an immersive, mission-oriented 3D educational game that transforms the scientific and engineering challenges of Mars exploration into an interactive learning experience. Rather than presenting space exploration solely through theoretical explanations, our project enables users to explore a simulated Martian research base, understand its essential infrastructure, and experience how astronauts interact with their surroundings.

How Does SOL 300 Work?

Players assume the role of an astronaut navigating a three-dimensional Martian environment through a third-person perspective. The research base consists of interconnected operational areas, each representing a different aspect of planetary exploration and human survival.

These environments include a vehicle hangar, a controlled greenhouse, crew living quarters, a mission control room, a laboratory, a medical facility, a support module, and an outdoor soil-data collection area. The simulation also features a location inspired by NASA's historic Phoenix Mars mission.

Through exploration and environmental interactions, players become familiar with the equipment, facilities, and procedures associated with operating a research station on Mars. The prototype establishes a foundation for more advanced missions involving scientific sample collection, greenhouse management, environmental monitoring, resource allocation, and crew safety.

Our proposed development framework extends these activities into interconnected mission scenarios in which decisions made within one operational system can influence other aspects of the research base.

Technologies and Development Tools

SOL 300 was developed using Unreal Engine and Blender, combining real-time 3D simulation with detailed environmental modeling.

Blender was used in the three-dimensional design and preparation of the Martian base, its architectural structures, and environmental assets. Unreal Engine was used to assemble the interactive environment, implement character navigation, integrate animations, and establish the gameplay framework.

The project integrates 3D modeling, animation, environment design, and interactive game development to create an immersive educational experience.

Our design approach emphasizes visual clarity, recognizable operational equipment, and spatial consistency, allowing players to understand the purpose of different facilities through direct exploration.

Scientific Foundations and NASA Technology Integration

A central feature of SOL 300 is its connection to established NASA research and technological developments.

The project draws inspiration from NASA's Phoenix mission, particularly its soil and ice investigation instruments, TEGA and MECA. These technologies provide the scientific foundation for proposed gameplay scenarios involving sample collection, laboratory examination, and resource assessment.

NASA's Perseverance rover also informs the project's environmental science concepts. Its MEDA instrument provides a reference for atmospheric monitoring, while the MOXIE experiment introduces the concept of oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere.

Additionally, NASA's Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) and space-based plant cultivation research provide the foundation for future gameplay involving water recovery, greenhouse operations, and sustainable resource management.

The project also explores how space-related technological developments, including thermal protection materials and infrared temperature measurement, can be integrated into educational scenarios involving astronaut health and safety.

These scientific references are intended to support meaningful interactions rather than serve as purely decorative elements.

Innovation and Creativity

The innovative aspect of SOL 300 lies in its approach to connecting multiple scientific disciplines within a unified interactive environment.

Conventional educational materials often introduce topics such as life-support systems, planetary geology, agriculture, and spacecraft technology separately. SOL 300 brings these subjects together within a shared Martian research base, helping users understand their practical relationships.

For example, a future mission could require players to collect a soil sample, investigate its characteristics in the laboratory, assess its potential relevance to greenhouse operations, and evaluate the resources necessary to support cultivation.

This approach transforms individual scientific concepts into interconnected operational decisions.

Another important creative element is the combination of scientifically inspired environments with accessible gameplay. Instead of requiring advanced technical knowledge, SOL 300 introduces complex engineering concepts through visual exploration, interaction, and progressively structured tasks.

Target Audience and Educational Benefits

SOL 300 primarily targets secondary school students, university students, STEM educators, and science enthusiasts interested in space exploration.

Its educational objective is to strengthen scientific curiosity, systems thinking, problem-solving abilities, and interdisciplinary understanding.

By presenting scientific concepts within an interactive environment, the project aims to help learners recognize how theoretical knowledge relates to real-world engineering challenges.

The simulation is also designed with future classroom integration in mind. Planned educational features include instructor-selected missions, adjustable difficulty levels, task-performance records, and pre- and post-activity assessments to evaluate learning outcomes.

Design Considerations and Future Development

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific relevance, educational accessibility, visual immersion, and the feasibility of implementing an interactive prototype within the competition's development period.

We also considered the importance of distinguishing currently implemented features from planned capabilities. The present prototype focuses on exploration, environmental design, character movement, and foundational interactions, while more advanced system simulations and mission dependencies form part of our development roadmap.

Our long-term vision is to transform SOL 300 into a modular educational platform that can be expanded to include lunar exploration, planetary resource management, emergency response scenarios, and advanced astronaut training concepts.

Future development could also support PC and virtual reality environments, enabling increasingly immersive educational experiences.

Intended Impact

SOL 300 aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and meaningful by allowing learners to experience the challenges of planetary exploration rather than simply read about them.

By combining NASA-inspired scientific knowledge, interactive simulation, and immersive game design, our project seeks to encourage curiosity, strengthen STEM education, and inspire young people to pursue careers in science, engineering, and space technology.

Ultimately, SOL 300 is not simply a game about living on Mars. It is a developing educational environment designed to help the next generation understand the scientific thinking, technological interdependence, and engineering decisions required to explore worlds beyond Earth.
